implemented.implementation: The T31 anytls security layer is shared: AnytlsSecurity/parse_anytls_security became TlsSecurity/parse_tls_security, TrojanOutbound carries the mode and trojan::wrap_security replaces the plain rustls handshake with shadow_tls::wrap. The trojan header then travels inside the ShadowTLS plaintext records. Version 0/2 and 1 load; version 3 stays rejected with the session-id reason.
Same shared parser; trojan::wrap_security uses tls_io::connect_jls with the parsed credentials. Required username/password and the ShadowTLS/JLS mutual exclusion match the pinned type.

Parsed into TlsSettings.client_fingerprint and applied as the T30/T32 rustls profile approximation (no uTLS ClientHello); empty/none keeps the standard handshake, like the pinned GetFingerprint fallback.

TrustTunnelUdp opens the pinned `_udp2` h2 CONNECT stream and carries `u32 length | source 16+2 | destination 16+2 | u8 app-name length | app name | payload`; replies are `u32 length | source 16+2 | local 16+2 | payload`. IPv4 uses the last four bytes of the 16-byte field, `::1` is not decoded as IPv4, a non-IP destination is resolved first (the pinned ResolveUDP), and one association serves every destination. `Proxy::udp_enabled()` reports it; the mixed inbound and the TUN data plane both build the association; a dialer-proxy chain loads (like T32's QUIC families) and the association refuses it by name.
Parsed into the shared TLS settings and applied as the rustls profile approximation.
Parsed and applied to the optional TLS layer as the rustls profile approximation; without `tls: true` the pinned client ignores it and the kernel accepts it the same way.

Validated (conservative/standard/aggressive) and mapped to quinn's BBR initial window through tuic::congestion_tuning_profile, the same documented approximation as T32's TUIC/ShadowQUIC rows. Exactly like the pinned SetCongestionController switch, the profile only changes behaviour together with a bbr controller; alone it loads and does nothing.

Accepted and mapped to quinn's BBR sender (closest available; the legacy meta v1 sender is absent). tuic::congestion_tuning now selects BBR for bbr_meta_v1 too, so TUIC/ShadowQUIC/masque agree; bbr-profile stays effective for bbr/bbr_meta_v2 only, matching the pinned switch.

KIP StartUot: the shared connect_stream learns Handshake::StartUot (features OPEN_TCP|UOT, TYPE_START_UOT after rekey), and SudokuUdp carries `u16 address length | u16 payload length | SOCKS5 address | payload` frames over that stream, reading the same layout back (address padding past the encoded form is tolerated). One association serves every destination. Proxy::udp_enabled() reports it; mixed inbound and TUN both build it; one SOCKS5 dialer-proxy hop is supported like the TCP path.

residuals.reason: The pinned h2 variant builds an HTTP/2 CONNECT-IP client (h2c-mode transport, capsulated CONNECT-IP over h2 DATA frames). The kernel implements CONNECT-IP over HTTP/3 only; an h2 CONNECT-IP carrier is a second capsule transport rather than an option mapping.

residuals.reason: The pinned ListenPacketContext dials the enfein/mieru client's stream and wraps it in NewUDPAssociateWrapper(NewPacketOverStreamTunnel(c)); that packet-over-stream framing lives in the external locked mieru module, not in a kernel implementation. The kernel's mieru is a clean-room TCP stream client with no packet/associate layer.
